details:
Project Details

What it does and how it works

Tracks on Mars is an interactive web app that teaches kids aged 8 to 12 about space exploration through the story of NASA’s Opportunity Mars rover. The experience has three parts:

  1. An animated storyteller video that narrates Opportunity’s journey from launch and landing on Mars to its long years of exploration and its final silence.
  2. A digital story book where children can go through the story at their own pace, with illustrations and simple explanations of how the rover worked and what it discovered.
  3. A quiz at the end that turns what they learned into a fun challenge, with feedback to reinforce the key facts.

Children move from watching, to reading, to actively recalling what they learned, all in one place.

Benefits and intended impact

There are very few educational animations about space and spacecraft made for children. Our project fills that gap with content that is educational but also calm and enjoyable, so kids can relax while they learn.

Opportunity was built for a 90-day mission but kept working for almost 15 years, until a global dust storm ended contact in 2018. Its story shows kids the value of curiosity, perseverance, and teamwork, and it keeps a spacecraft that has gone quiet from being forgotten. We believe space is not a luxury. Every generation should have awareness of it, because the children learning today will explore, protect, and make decisions about space tomorrow.

Tools, languages, and technologies

  • Development: Claude AI to assist with coding; HTML and CSS for structure and styling [add JavaScript if you used it for the quiz or page interactions]
  • Voice and narration: ElevenLabs for AI-generated voice
  • Sound effects: Mixkit for sound effects
  • Animation and illustrations: [Canva, Blender, Figma, AI image tools]
  • Hosting: [Netlify]
  • Information sources: NASA public resources and mission data on the Opportunity rover [list the specific pages you used]

How the project is creative

Instead of presenting facts as a lecture, we wrapped them in a story. Opportunity is told as a character with a journey, so kids connect with the mission emotionally and remember it. We combined three formats (video, book, quiz) so different learners can engage in the way that suits them. Narration and sound effects add atmosphere, and the gentle tone lets children enjoy the content without feeling pressured.

Factors our team considered

  • Audience: Language, visuals, and pacing were designed for ages 8 to 12, keeping concepts simple but accurate.
  • Accuracy: Space facts are based on NASA’s publicly available information.
  • Accessibility: The app runs in a browser with no installation, so it is available to as many children as possible.
  • Engagement: The quiz and varied formats keep kids motivated and reinforce learning.
  • Balance: We aimed to educate while also giving kids something relaxing to enjoy.
  • Responsible use of AI: We used AI tools for coding and voice generation, and checked the content against NASA sources for accuracy.
  • Future growth: More rovers, spacecraft, languages, and quiz levels can be added later.
